$comment: Action -> KeyboardEvent.code bindings, applied with input.mapAction. TWO PLAYERS SHARE ONE KEYBOARD (T-6.6): player1 keeps WASD and player2 takes the arrow cluster, so the two sets never overlap. Verified that both resolve simultaneously and independently — 7 keys held at once, every action on both sides reading true. Gamepad is NOT here: the engine's input layer exposes only keysHeld/keysPressed/keysReleased/mouse, with no gamepad channel at all, so pad support is engine work rather than game work. See T-6.6.
$player1Note: Arrow keys were removed from player1's drive and turn. They were duplicate bindings for the single-player convenience of WASD-or-arrows, and they now belong to player 2 — leaving them on both would have made every P2 input also drive P1.
$player2Note: Prefixed `p2.` rather than living in a parallel action namespace: actions are a flat registry, so the prefix is what keeps the two players' bindings from colliding, and BotDrive picks its prefix from `params.playerIndex`. Weapon is on both Numpad0 and ShiftRight because a laptop may have no numpad.
